ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit. The input voltage u_i is connected through a resistor labeled 1 kΩ to the inverting input node of the op-amp; the op-amp output terminal u_o is fed back through a resistor labeled 10 kΩ to the same inverting input node; the non-inverting input terminal is grounded through resistor R′. Negative feedback is formed from the output through 10 kΩ back to the inverting terminal. Reasoning: When an ideal op-amp operates with negative feedback, the potentials of the inverting input terminal and the non-inverting input terminal are equal. Since the non-inverting input terminal is grounded through R′, the inverting input terminal can be regarded as virtual ground. This circuit is a standard inverting amplifier, and the voltage gain is A_v = u_o/u_i = -R_f/R_in = -10 kΩ/1 kΩ = -10.
